title: US Tax Withholding on Earnings Released to Payout Methods
content:
When the host account's taxpayer form status is "not provided", US tax is withheld from every release of earnings to the host's Payout Methods. The rate depends on the host's tax residency on the host account.

## The rule

- A host whose tax residency is **US** has the backup withholding rate (24.00% on every rail) withheld.
- A host whose tax residency is **non-US** has the nonresident withholding rate (30.00% on every rail) withheld.
- Each is taken on the withholding base, the earnings released for the stay or installment before payout-method fees, and rounded to the nearest cent, half up.
- No withholding is taken while a W-9 (US residency) or a W-8 (non-US residency) is on file.
- Withholding is taken once per release and is never refunded by support once taken; it is credited against the host's annual US tax return through the year-end tax form.
- A form supplied later stops withholding on releases from that day onward only.

## How the amount is formed

The withholding on a release is the release amount multiplied by the applicable rate, divided by one hundred, and rounded half up to the cent.

| Taxpayer form status on the host account | Tax residency | Withholding on each release |
|---|---|---|
| Not provided | US | 24.00% of the release, rounded half up to the cent |
| Not provided | Non-US | 30.00% of the release, rounded half up to the cent |
| W-9 on file | US | None |
| W-8 on file | Non-US | None |

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

- An imagined US host with no form on file has USD 1028.20 released. 24.00% of USD 1028.20 is USD 246.768, rounded half up to USD 246.77.
- An imagined non-US host with no form on file has USD 455.15 released. 30.00% of USD 455.15 is USD 136.545, rounded half up to USD 136.55.
- An imagined US host with no form on file has two releases withheld on in March, then supplies a W-9 on April 3. A release on April 3 or later carries no withholding; the two March withholdings stay as taken and are credited through the year-end tax form.

## Once per release

Each withholding names the release it is taken on. Where the payout ledger already shows a withholding naming that release, no second withholding is taken on it.

## Points of judgement

- *Can support refund withholding already taken?* No. Once taken, withholding is never refunded by support; it is credited against the host's annual US tax return through the year-end tax form.
- *Does a transfer fee reduce the amount withholding is computed on?* No. The base is the released earnings before payout-method fees.
